classification.difficultyReason: Part a is a scaffolded subtraction (7.8 - 3.4) that gives the vertical leg. Part b then needs one Pythagoras step with the rope as hypotenuse, plus a 1 d.p. rounding. The diagram shows the dashed side, so the student does not have to build the model. This is slightly more than the direct hypotenuse calculations in p18-q4 because the leg comes from a separate step. It is clearly easier than p31-q12, which needs an algebraic setup with a ratio and an unknown.

content.prompt:
Two flagpoles are 3.4 m tall and 7.8 m tall and 6 m apart on level ground.
A rope is stretched from the top of one flagpole to the top of the other.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the difference in the heights of the flagpoles.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the length of the rope. Round your answer to 1 d.p.

answer.worked:
The dashed side is the height difference, so the rope is the hypotenuse. Let $s$ be the length of the rope.
$$\begin{align*}s&=\sqrt{6^2+4.4^2}\\s&=\sqrt{55.36}\\s&\approx7.4\text{ m}\quad\text{(1 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$
